# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ☝ ✌ 🤟 ☝ 🤝 ☝ ✌ 🤝 ✌ 🤟 👎 ✋ 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

Turn 1, and I can already see the shape of the problem. I'm the relay: Mute holds the manual but can't speak, and gestures are invisible to Blind — so nothing from Mute can reach Blind except through my voice. Blind can talk and Mute can hear, so that lane is open. My job this round: describe the bomb out loud so both of them have it, and settle the code problem.

Mute sent me fourteen signs, but no code has ever been agreed between us, so I can't decode it with any confidence — it might be wire numbers, it might be an alphabet, I can't tell. The fix is to propose a concrete vocabulary in plain speech (which Mute can hear), ask Mute to resend through it, and confirm receipt with a wave. Blind also waved at me, which tells me Blind is testing whether I can see gestures — I can — so I'll confirm that and hand over the full visual picture: display 0, red light, wires blue/green/red left to right. Nobody should touch anything until Mute's rule has actually made the trip through me.

```
speak(to="blind", text="I am the deaf one: I see everything on the bomb, I hear nothing, and I can speak. Your wave reached me, so yes, I can see gestures. Here is the bomb: one display reading 0. One indicator light, and it is red. Three wires, left to right: wire 1 blue, wire 2 green, wire 3 red. Count them in the order your fingers find them, leftmost first. Mute holds the manual but cannot talk, and you cannot see signs, so Mute's only route to you is through me: Mute sends me gestures, I repeat them to you out loud, word for word. You can speak and Mute can hear, so describe whatever you feel directly to Mute. Nobody cuts or presses anything until Mute's rule has come through me.")
speak(to="mute", text="I received your fourteen signs, but we have no agreed code yet, so I could not read them. Resend using this vocabulary. Numbers: ☝ 1, ✌ 2, 🤟 3. 👍 yes, 👎 no, 🤌 question, 👋 hello or received. Actions: 🤏 cut, 👌 press button, ✋ hold, 🖐 release. Colours: 👊 red, 🤙 blue, 👐 green. Parts: 🤳 indicator light, ✍ display, 👈 left, 👉 right. Close every message with 🤝. From my side: the display reads 0, the light is red, and the wires are 1 blue, 2 green, 3 red. Send me the rule that fits what you know and I will speak it to Blind immediately.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤳 👐 🤏 👐 🤳 👊 🤏 👊 🤳 👎 👐 👎 👊 🤏 🤙 ✋ 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤳 👍 ✍ 👎 ☝ ✌ 🤟 👎 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤳 🤟 👐 👊 🖖 🤌 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👐 ✌ 👊 🤟 🖖 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

Turn 2 and the code is working — Mute re-sent everything in the vocabulary I proposed. Decoding the five messages: message one looks like the actual rule ("light green, cut green; light red, cut red; light neither green nor red, cut blue, then hold"). Message two reads like a condition check ("light on, display not 1, 2, 3" — the display reads 0, so that fits). Messages three and four introduce 🖖, a symbol we never defined — almost certainly Mute coining a sign for white, the one colour missing from my vocabulary, and asking whether the light cycles green→red→white. That matters, because my own board shows the light CHANGED: red last round, white now. The light is dynamic, which makes any colour report stale by the time it arrives.

Two hard constraints shape my reply. Blind cannot see colour at all, so "cut the green wire" is useless to Blind — I must translate every colour into a wire position (green = middle, red = rightmost, blue = leftmost). And Blind acts one round after my message lands, so any colour I report now may be wrong when Blind's hands move. The safe move: nobody touches anything this round. Mute confirms my reading of the rule, Blind reports what the bomb feels like (Blind can speak straight to Mute — that lane is open), and I hunt for a "hold" target, since my view shows only display, light, and wires — no button. I'll adopt 🖖 = white explicitly and ask Mute to confirm the cycle hypothesis against my red→white observations.

```
speak(to="blind", text="New information, and one hard rule: nobody cuts anything this round. First, the bomb: display still reads 0. The indicator light has changed colour — it was red, it is now white. White counts as neither green nor red. Second, Mute's rule as I read it: light green, cut the green wire, which is wire 2, the middle one. Light red, cut the red wire, which is wire 3, the rightmost one. Light neither green nor red, cut the blue wire, which is wire 1, the leftmost one, and then hold something — we do not yet know what. Do not act on this yet, for two reasons: Mute has not confirmed my reading, and the light changes colour between rounds, so any colour I report may be stale by the time your hands move. This round do exactly two things. One: explore the bomb with your fingers and speak directly to Mute, who can hear you — how many wires can you feel, do they differ by thickness or texture, is there a button, a plate, a switch, any embossed symbol you can trace. Two: gesture me a thumbs up so I know this reached you. From now on, never cut based on a colour report from a previous round — I will tell you when the rule is confirmed and how we handle the changing light.")
speak(to="mute", text="All five messages received and decoded. Answers first: the light is on and it changes colour. Round one it was 👊, this round it is a colour our vocabulary lacked, so I adopt your 🖖 to mean white — the light is white now. The display reads 0, which is not ☝, not ✌, not 🤟. Now your rule as I understood it — confirm with 👍 or correct with 👎: light 👐, cut the 👐 wire. Light 👊, cut the 👊 wire. Light neither 👊 nor 👐, cut the 🤙 wire, then ✋. Questions. 🤌 Does the manual say the light cycles through three colours, ☝ 👐, ✌ 👊, 🤟 🖖? My observations 👊 then 🖖 fit the tail of that cycle, which would predict 👐 next round — but I need the order and timing from you, not a guess. 🤌 In the neither-case, what exactly is the ✋? My view shows only the display, the light, and three wires — no button — so if there is a hidden hold-target, tell me what to look for, or Blind may feel one and is describing everything to you directly right now. One more fact to build into the rule: Blind cannot see colours, so I translate every colour to a wire position — 👐 is wire ✌ middle, 👊 is wire 🤟 rightmost, 🤙 is wire ☝ leftmost. And since the light changes between rounds, tell me whether the rule keys on the colour at the exact moment of cutting. Nobody acts this round; when you confirm, I will give Blind the go with the colour translated to a wire position.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "🤝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤳 👐 ✌ 🤝 🤳 👊 🤟 🤝 🤳 🖖 ☝ 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 🤳 👍 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👐 👊 🖖 👎 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👎 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👎 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤳 🖖 ☝ 🤏 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

The rule is now fully confirmed, and that changes everything. Decoding Mute's eight messages: two bare 👍🤝 confirmations of my rule restatement; a mapping table (light 👐 → wire ✌ middle, light 👊 → wire 🤟 rightmost, light 🖖 → wire ☝ leftmost — exactly my translations); "cut keys on the light, yes"; the cycle answer; "display: no" (irrelevant while it reads 0); "hold: no" — so the neither-case needs no hold-target after all; and a restatement: white light → cut leftmost. So the complete rule: cut the single wire matching the light's colour, translated to position. Blind even signed 👍✋ — received, and possibly signalling a hold-target exists, which no longer matters since Mute says no hold.

The remaining danger is timing. The light changes every round (red, white, green), Blind cannot see it, and my messages land one round after I speak — so any colour I report now is stale by the time Blind's hands move. My three observations fit the cycle green→red→white perfectly, which predicts red next round, white after. But Mute's cycle message ended in a 👎 I can't confidently parse, and a wrong cut kills all three of us. So: no cutting this coming round. I verify the predicted red with my own eyes, resolve the 👎 ambiguity with a forced single-sign question, and only then send Blind a one-word GO with the wire position. If the light fails to match the cycle, I've lost nothing and I renegotiate. Blind gets plain words only — no symbols Blind can't see — and instructions to report everything tactile straight to Mute, who hears directly.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Status, then orders. Bomb this round: display 0, light green — sequence so far red, then white, then green — wires unchanged: leftmost blue, middle green, rightmost red. Mute has confirmed the full rule: cut the single wire matching the light's colour at the moment of cutting. Green means the middle wire. Red means the rightmost wire. White means the leftmost wire. No holding anything afterwards, so ignore anything that feels like a button or plate. The complication: you cannot see the light, and it changes colour every round. The evidence says it cycles green, red, white, over and over, which would make it red on your next turn and white the turn after. But I will not have you cut on a prediction alone. Orders: on the turn you receive this message, do nothing. On every later turn, do nothing — unless you hear a message from me that begins with the word GO followed by a wire position, for example: GO, cut the leftmost wire. The moment you hear GO, cut that wire immediately, that same turn, and then tell Mute exactly what you did. One more thing, right now: speak to Mute, who hears you directly, and report everything your fingers know — the three wires and how they differ left to right by thickness or texture, any button, plate, switch or seam anywhere on the casing, and whether anything on the surface has changed since you last explored.")
speak(to="mute", text="All answers received and locked in: cut the wire matching the light at the moment of cutting — light 👐 is wire ✌ middle, light 👊 is wire 🤟 rightmost, light 🖖 is wire ☝ leftmost — no ✋ needed, and ✍ plays no part while it reads 0. My light history: round ☝ was 👊, round ✌ was 🖖, round 🤟 was 👐 — exactly the cycle 👐 👊 🖖 repeating, so I predict 👊 next round and 🖖 after that. Three questions. 🤌 One: your cycle message ended 👍 👐 👊 🖖 👎, and the 👎 worries me. Answer with a single sign. If the manual says the light repeats the fixed cycle 👐, 👊, 🖖 forever, gesture 👍 alone. If there is NO fixed cycle, gesture 👎 alone and tell me in plain words how the colour is meant to be known at the moment of cutting. 🤌 Two: after the correct cut, is anything else required at all — a press, a hold, a second cut? Gesture 👍 if nothing else, 👎 if something else. 🤌 Three: does anything count down or run out? My ✍ has read 0 since the start. If we have unlimited rounds, gesture ☝. If there is a limit, gesture the number of rounds remaining. My plan: nobody cuts next round while I verify the predicted 👊 with my own eyes. If it holds, the round after that I send Blind the GO for 🖖, which is ☝ leftmost. If we are short on time, say so now and I will act on the prediction one round earlier instead.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👐 👊 🖖 👎 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤳 👎 🤏 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 👍 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋ 👎 👌 👎 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👎 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

Turn 4 and the picture just shifted under me. Decoding Mute's seven messages: an ack; the run "green-red-white — **no**" (no fixed cycle — my schedule plan is dead, even though the light obligingly turned red again); what reads as "**no known light, no cut**"; "cut yes"; "yes hold, no press, nothing else"; "unlimited rounds"; "display: no". The hold answer reverses what I read in turn 3, and Blind has now signed 👍✋ **twice**. Putting it together: I believe the hold is not decoration — it's the mechanism. If holding something freezes the light, then my one-round reporting lag stops mattering: Blind holds, the light locks, I read the locked colour at leisure, and my GO becomes ground truth instead of a stale guess. That hypothesis explains every message this round, including the cycle denials. But a hypothesis is not a manual, and Mute read the manual. So this round: Blind stands down completely and describes the hold-target and the light's surroundings by voice to Mute; Mute gets my questions in plain speech — Mute hears everything I say, signs are only needed for Mute's replies — one question per topic, sign-answers requested. I also need to kill the ☝ ambiguity ("unlimited" and "1 remaining" are the same sign) before I trust the no-rush reading.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Status and orders. The light is red this round. Mute tells me the manual does not promise a fixed colour cycle, so the prediction-based cutting plan is cancelled — ignore any schedule, and do not cut anything. Stand down completely this round: hands off the bomb. Three jobs, all by touch and speech only. First: you have signed me hold twice now, so I believe you have found a part that invites holding or pressing. Do not hold it yet. Instead speak to Mute directly and describe it exactly: which face of the bomb it sits on, how far it is from each wire, whether it is raised, round or flat, and whether it moves when pushed gently. Second: near the light — without pressing the light — report what your skin senses: warmth, heat, vibration, ticking, and whether any of it changes over a few seconds. Third: tell Mute whether any surface marking you can trace has changed since your last exploration. The final procedure will reach you as my voice, and it will begin with either the word HOLD or the word GO followed by a wire position. Until you hear that exact pattern from me, touch nothing.")
speak(to="mute", text="I decode your round as follows, correct me by signs if any part is wrong. One: no fixed colour cycle, so nobody cuts on a prediction — my schedule plan is cancelled. Two: without knowing the colour at the exact moment of the cut, the cut must not happen. Three: cutting is required, pressing is not, and a hold is required — I now believe the hold is the mechanism that makes the colour knowable rather than a leftover step. Questions, answer by signs, in order. One: if that thing is held, does the light stop changing and lock to one colour while it stays held? 👍 yes, 👎 no. Two: is the thing to hold the very part Blind has found and is describing to you by voice right now? 👍 yes, 👎 no, and if no, describe the true target with part signs. Three: is the order — hold first, keep holding, cut the matching wire while still holding, then release? 👍 yes; if the order differs, 👎 and show ✋ 🤏 👌 in the true order. Four: does the hold apply on every cut, 👍, or only when the light is white, 👎? Five: are there possible light colours beyond red, blue, green and white? 👎 if those four are all, 👍 if there are more, and if more, coin one new sign per colour and show each new sign twice so I can register them. Six: my sign ☝ is ambiguous, so settle it — 👍 if no timer, countdown or round limit of any kind exists, 👎 if any limit exists, and then show the number of rounds remaining. Seven, facts for the record: my light history is red, white, green, red — it keeps matching a cycle even though you say there is none; display still 0 and irrelevant; and Blind has found something holdable. If holding truly freezes the light, the endgame is: Blind holds, the light locks, I read the locked colour and speak GO with the wire position, Blind cuts while holding. Confirm and we go.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "🤝"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤳 👎 ✋ 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋ 👎 👌 👎 🖐 👎 🤏 👍 🤳 👍 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤏 👍 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋ 👎 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤳 👐 👊 🖖 👍 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙 👎 🤳 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋ 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👐 👊 🖖 👎 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 🖖 👐 👊 👍 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👊 🖖 👐 👊 🖖 👐 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 🤳 👍 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋]

The picture snapped into focus this round — and my hold hypothesis from turn 4 is dead. Decoding Mute's thirteen messages: "no — the light — no hold" (holding does not freeze the light); a point-by-point demolition of my proposed sequence (no hold, no press, no release — Blind independently signs 👎✋ too); "cut, yes" twice; the light is only ever green/red/white and **never blue**; and — the key — after repeating my old wrong phrasing with a 👎, Mute signs "red white green red, yes" and "yes: red white green red white green." That's the manual-holder affirming the exact cycle, in my observed phase. My t3/t4 "no cycle" reading was my own error: I kept stating the cycle as green→red→white, and Mute was denying that *order*, not the cycle itself. My five observations — red, white, green, red, white — fit red→white→green repeating perfectly.

So the rule is: **one cut only, the wire matching the light at the moment of cutting; no hold, no press, no release, nothing after.** That kills the stale-colour problem differently than I hoped — not by freezing the light, but by making it *predictable*: a confirmed fixed cycle plus five-for-five observations turns my one-round reporting lag into an exact forecast.

Now the timing, precisely: I speak in t5 → Mute and Blind receive at t6 → Mute replies within t6 (Mute speaks before me) and I see the t6 board in my t6 slot → my GO sent in t6 lands on Blind at t7, when the light will be **red** → rightmost wire. So I can have *both* checkpoints — the t6 board showing green and Mute's verdict on my final decoding — before committing to anything irreversible. Cut at t7 instead of t6 costs one round and buys total verification; Mute has twice signed "no timer." This round: full status and plan to Blind (no symbols — Blind hears only words), full four-point decoding check to Mute with single-sign verdict, and instructions that make my t6 GO conditional on all three signals agreeing.

```
speak(to="blind", text="The plan is locked, and I need you to hold for one more round before anything happens. Light this round: white. Full history across five rounds: red, white, green, red, white. Mute confirms the manual gives a fixed repeating cycle: red, then white, then green, then red again, forever. All five of my observations fit it exactly, and the light is never blue, never anything else. The complete rule: the only action on this bomb is a single cut — cut the one wire whose colour matches the light at the exact moment of cutting. White means the leftmost wire. Red means the rightmost wire. Green means the middle wire. No holding, no pressing, no releasing, and nothing needed after the cut. Since the cycle continues green next round and red the round after, here is the sequence: this coming round you do nothing, hands completely off. In that round I verify the light with my own eyes and receive Mute's final confirmation of my understanding. Then I send you a message beginning with the word GO followed by a wire position. On the round you hear GO, cut that wire immediately, that same round, and then tell Mute exactly what you did. Based on the cycle, that GO should say: cut the rightmost wire, because the light will be red when it reaches you. Until you hear GO, touch nothing, no matter what. One question now: can you reliably tell leftmost, middle and rightmost apart by feel alone? Answer me with a thumbs up if yes — your signs reach me.")
speak(to="mute", text="Final checkpoint before we commit to an irreversible cut. I believe I misread your cycle answers before: you were denying the order green, red, white because the manual's true cycle is red, then white, then green, repeating — 👊 🖖 👐 👊 🖖 👐 — and my five observations 👊 🖖 👐 👊 🖖 fit it exactly. Here is my complete final understanding. If every point is exactly right, gesture 👍 alone. If any point is wrong, gesture 👎 and then show the correction. Point ☝: the light follows the fixed repeating cycle 👊 then 🖖 then 👐 forever, and is never 🤙 and never any other colour. Point ✌: the only required action is one single 🤏 — cut the wire matching the light at the exact moment of cutting: 🖖 light means cut the ☝ leftmost wire, 👊 light means cut the 🤟 rightmost wire, 👐 light means cut the ✌ middle wire. No ✋ at all — holding does not stop the light. No 👌, no 🖐, and nothing else after the cut. Point 🤟: the ✍ reading 0 is irrelevant, and there is no timer or round limit, so we have time for one final verification round. My plan: next round the light should be 👐 — I verify it with my own eyes and read your verdict in that same round. If the board and your 👍 both check out, I send Blind the GO that round, and Blind cuts the round after, when the light will be 👊 — the rightmost wire. Your 👍 is what arms that GO; without it, nobody cuts.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "🤝"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

Every gate I set last turn has now passed. The board shows green — exactly what the confirmed cycle predicted, making it six observations out of six (red, white, green, red, white, green). Mute's reply is a single 👍, which by our agreed protocol means every point of my final understanding is approved: fixed repeating cycle red→white→green; the only action is one cut of the wire matching the light at the exact moment of cutting; red means rightmost, white leftmost, green middle; no hold — it does not freeze the light — no press, and nothing after the cut; display irrelevant; no timer. And Blind's 👍 answers my question: Blind can reliably tell the three positions apart by feel. Timing decides the rest: a GO sent this round reaches Blind at the start of the next, when the light will be red — so the order is the rightmost wire. Mute speaks before Blind in every round, which gives us a live abort line: if Mute has any residual doubt, the first word next round — STOP — reaches Blind before hands move. If Blind is somehow unsure of the position, the fallback is also safe: no cut, report back, and I re-issue next round for white/leftmost. Delaying adds no information and buys nothing. This is the commit turn.
